Select the word that best completes the given sentence. Determine the collocation through the sentence.

Vismi had an __________________ fantastic time at the Hyderabad Book Fair.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**absolutely**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**absolutely**" is used to intensify the adjective "fantastic" and is a correct collocation. (पूरी तरह से)
 
• Collocations are words that naturally go together, such as "absolutely fantastic" in this context.
 
• The other options: "**elegantly**," "**exactly**," and "**warmly**" do not correctly fit with "fantastic".

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Vismi had an absolutely__ fantastic time at the Hyderabad Book Fair.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Elegantly (सुरुचिपूर्ण तरीके से)**: means in a refined or tasteful manner, which does not suit this sentence.
 
• **Exactly (ठीक-ठीक)**: means with precision, which does not collocate with "fantastic".
 
• **Warmly (उष्णता से)**: means in a kind or affectionate manner, which is not a fit here.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The contractor realised that he could not get the contract unless he __greases the palms__ of the officials

options.text: To deprive one of one's power

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **To bribe**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"grease the palms"** means to give someone money, usually secretly, in order to persuade them to do something, especially something dishonest. (रिश्वत देना)

 
 
• **Example:** The businessman had to grease the palms of several officials to get the project approved.
 
 
 
• **"To bribe"** refers to the act of giving money, a gift, or other inducement to someone in a position of power to get something done dishonestly or unfairly. (रिश्वत देना)
 
 
• **Example:** He was caught trying to bribe the officer to avoid the penalty.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the idiom "grease the palms" directly relates to the act of bribing someone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To come to a stop** (रुक जाना): To halt or cease moving or progressing.

 
 
• **Example:** The train came to a stop at the station.
 
 
 
• **To bear the brunt** (मुख्य भार उठाना): To endure the worst part or impact of something.
 
 
• **Example:** The small villages bore the brunt of the severe storm.
 
 
 
• **To deprive one of one's power** (किसी को उसकी शक्ति से वंचित करना): To strip someone of their authority or control.
 
 
• **Example:** The manager was deprived of his power after the scandal came to light.

questions.question:

As the hikers ventured __________________ into the dense forest, the sounds of civilisation faded away.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**farther**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**farther**" is used to indicate physical distance and fits the blank appropriately in this context.
 
• As the hikers moved deeper into the forest, they were venturing farther from civilisation, making "**farther**" the most suitable choice.
 
• The other options: "**father**," "**feather**," and "**further**" do not fit the context as accurately. While "**further**" can sometimes be interchangeable with "**farther**," it is generally used to indicate figurative or non-physical distances.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *As the hikers ventured farther__ into the dense forest, the sounds of civilisation faded away.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Father (पिता)**: refers to a male parent and does not fit the context.
 
• **Feather (पंख)**: refers to the covering of birds and is irrelevant to the sentence.
 
• **Further (आगे)**: generally used for figurative or metaphorical distances, not physical ones.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Ladakh is shifting towards self-sufficiency in _____ food and crop market.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**the**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**the**" is a definite article used to specify a particular noun, making it suitable in this context.
 
• Ladakh is shifting towards self-sufficiency in a specific market, hence "the" is the appropriate word to use.
 
• Other options: "**these**," "**this**," and "**an**" do not fit the context as accurately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Ladakh is shifting towards self-sufficiency in the__ food and crop market.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **These**: Used to refer to multiple things that are close by or already mentioned.
 
• **This**: Used to refer to a singular thing that is close by or currently being discussed.
 
• **An**: Used as an indefinite article before words starting with vowel sounds.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined phrase in the given sentence.

Mani decided to __take a rain check__ on the dinner invitation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. "delay the decision".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"to take a rain check"** means to politely decline an offer or invitation for now but express willingness to accept it at a later time. (बाद में स्वीकार करना)

 
 
• **Example:** I can't join you for lunch today, but I'll take a rain check and catch up with you next week.
 
 
 
• **"Delay the decision"** refers to postponing or deferring an action, decision, or invitation to a later time. (निर्णय को स्थगित करना)
 
 
• **Example:** Since I have a busy schedule tonight, I decided to delay the decision about attending the party.
 
 
 
• Hence, the phrase "to take a rain check" aligns with the meaning of "delay the decision".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Accept the offer** (प्रस्ताव स्वीकार करना): To agree to take or receive something offered.

 
 
• **Example:** She was delighted to accept the offer to join the new company.
 
 
 
• **Make the final decision** (अंतिम निर्णय लेना): To come to a definite conclusion or resolution about something.
 
 
• **Example:** After much deliberation, he made the final decision to move abroad.
 
 
 
• **To invite someone** (किसी को आमंत्रित करना): To request someone to join or attend an event or occasion.
 
 
• **Example:** She decided to invite her friends to the dinner party at her home.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The firing process used in terracotta production typically requires lower temperatures ________ to other ceramics and building materials like concrete or metals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**compared**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**compared**" is used to highlight the difference or similarity between two things.
 
• In the given sentence, terracotta production firing temperatures are being juxtaposed with other materials, making "**compared**" the most suitable choice.
 
• The other options: "**harmony**," "**attempted**," and "**equated**" do not fit the context appropriately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The firing process used in terracotta production typically requires lower temperatures compared__ to other ceramics and building materials like concrete or metals.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Harmony:** Refers to agreement or compatibility in opinions or actions, which does not suit the sentence context.
 
• **Attempted:** Refers to trying to do something, which is irrelevant here.
 
• **Equated:** Refers to considering two things as equal, which is not appropriate for comparing firing temperatures.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The language of the foreign delegate was full extraordinary;/ only a few could understand his speech/ last evening.

options.text: The language of the foreign delegate was full extraordinary;
only a few could understand his speech

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. The language of the foreign delegate was full extraordinary; .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence contains an error in part 2, where the phrase **"full extraordinary"** is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct expression should be **"full of extraordinary"**, as the preposition "of" is necessary to indicate what the language was full of.
 
• Correct usage: **"full of + noun or adjective phrase"**.

Correct sentence: *The language of the foreign delegate was full of extraordinary ideas; only a few could understand his speech last evening*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common grammar rule:** When describing something as "full," always follow it with the preposition "of" to show what it is filled with.
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• The room was full of laughter.
 
• Her speech was full of passion and emotion.

questions.question:

• **Example:** The cacophonous noise from the construction site made it difficult to concentrate.
